card.law_is_about: Mandatory three-month retention of IP-address assignment data and other digital investigation powers.
card.they_want: Oppose indiscriminate retention and require stronger justification for the proposed powers.
card.they_claim: Germany had effectively conducted no data retention for over 18 years by January 2026.
card.the_problem: Actual retained data existed under the 2008 regime before the March 2010 judgment; the latest continuous gap then measured less than 16 years.

locator.section: Opening factual account, paragraph beginning Aufgrund der einstweiligen Anordnungen des Ersten Senats
locator.paragraph_context: Refers to interim orders19March2008and6November2008; precedes Die Beschwerdeführer

correction: The court describes data already stored under the 2007 statute and the 2008 interim restrictions on their use. The regime operated before the 2 March 2010 judgment invalidated it. January 2026 is less than 16 years after that date, so a continuous absence of actual retention for over 18 years is incorrect. This does not assert uninterrupted implementation by every provider before 2010 or disregard interim use restrictions.
effect: Slightly weakens the length-of-experience premise used to question necessity. The long subsequent period without the invalidated regime remains; no claimed change in crime clearance follows from correcting this date.
limits: Minor chronology issue only. The statement says de facto, so this is checked against actual stored data rather than merely a statute’s existence. One possible loose reading is that no fully constitutionally valid retention scheme existed; that differs from the express claim that no retention was conducted. The correction does not establish necessity, proportionality, legality, effectiveness or appropriate duration of the 2025 draft. Its separate 90.8% clearance quotation and broader rights objections are not refuted.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the overstatement is a little over two years in a subsidiary historical premise, and the much longer absence since 2010 still supports discussing alternatives. No substantive legal conclusion turns on 18 rather than fewer than 16 years.
direction_explanation: True, narrowly: a longer claimed period without retention makes the stated demand for a necessity justification appear stronger. This says nothing about intention or whether the requested policy is sound.
context_checks: Read complete 13-page response, including its distinction between indiscriminate storage, targeted preservation and later access; checked paragraphs before and after the historical claim.
Verified relevant page 4 text against ministry-hosted 28 January copy and author-hosted copy. Cover contributor lists differ; substantive claim/request agree.
Read primary court summary including explicit references to stored data and interim restrictions; do not confuse restricted disclosure with no storage.

The summary also says the draft contains no necessity explanation, while page 7 acknowledges the draft’s page 53 praxis-experience statement and argues it lacks empirical support. This concerns adequacy of justification and is not promoted as another factual error.

draft.date_note: Draft publication date, not an inferred signed preparation date; 61 pages in the official download. Submission cover gives January 2026, exact day from ministry archive filename.
draft.relevant_provisions: Article 6, proposed section 176 TKG, physical PDF pages 12–13; explanatory text pages 50–54. Response explicitly cites draft pages 28/53 and the matching proposed provisions.
draft.version_check: The December consultation draft is compared, not later cabinet or Bundestag amendments.

history.event: First recorded as narrow provisional chronology finding after source-context and exact-draft checks; independent review requested.
Independent review retained minor/true and added contemporaneous operational corroboration from official BT 16/11139. Main court quote shortened; no additional author quotation.

supplementary_counter_quote.original: In 934 dieser Verfahren mussten die um Auskunft ersuchten Telekommunikationsunternehmen auch auf nach § 113a TKG gespeicherte Daten zurückgreifen.
supplementary_counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: In 934 of these proceedings, the telecommunications companies asked for information also had to draw on data stored under section 113a TKG.

locator.section: Answer to question 2, first paragraph; May–July 2008 survey

operational_corroboration: The contemporaneous government answer reports actual use of section 113a data in 934 of 2,186 surveyed proceedings, and separately records partial noncompliance in answer 4 on page 5. This establishes operation rather than merely a statutory duty, without proving that retention caused any case to be solved.
